features.name: monthly_payment_burden
features.description: Approximate monthly payment as credit_amount divided by duration months.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a key threshold for separating affordable vs heavy obligations; trees can split on payment size.

features.name: log_credit_amount
features.description: Log-transformed credit amount to compress the right tail for cleaner threshold splits.
features.expected_model_benefit: Stabilizes scale of loan size; provides more uniform split points for tree algorithms.

features.name: long_duration_flag
features.description: Indicator that the loan duration exceeds 24 months, capturing long-horizon risk exposure.
features.expected_model_benefit: Clean boolean split for long-term loans which often associate with higher default risk.

features.name: duration_bucket
features.description: Ordinal bucket of loan duration: 0=<=12, 1=13-24, 2=25-36, 3=37-48, 4=>48 months.
features.expected_model_benefit: Predefined nonlinear duration bins help trees segment risk tiers efficiently.

features.name: age_bucket
features.expected_model_benefit: Life-stage groupings capture nonlinear effects of age on creditworthiness.

features.name: young_high_installment
features.description: Interaction: applicant under 30 with installment commitment of 3 or more (high relative burden).
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures vulnerable demographic with high income-share commitment as one tree-friendly indicator.

features.name: no_checking_flag
features.description: Indicator for applicants who have no checking account on file.
features.expected_model_benefit: Strong known signal in this dataset; isolates a clean categorical split.

features.name: negative_checking_flag
features.description: Indicator for applicants with negative checking account balance (<0).
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures financial stress signal independent of other checking categories.

features.name: low_savings_flag
features.description: Indicator that savings are below 100 (lowest known savings bucket).
features.expected_model_benefit: Identifies thin financial cushion, a key risk threshold for trees.

features.name: amount_per_installment_unit
features.description: Credit amount scaled by installment commitment level, proxying total income-relative load.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines two predictive features; useful nonlinear interaction for tree splits.

features.name: applicant_stability_score
features.description: Semantic 0-5 ordinal score of applicant stability combining housing ownership, employment tenure, residence duration, and job skill level. Higher = more stable. Computed as sum of: own housing (+1), employment >=4 years (+1), employment >=7 years (+1 additional), residence_since >=3 (+1), skilled or high-qualif job (+1).
features.expected_model_benefit: Encodes domain notion of life stability as a single ordinal that trees can threshold cleanly.

features.name: credit_profile_risk_score
features.description: Semantic 0-4 ordinal risk score from credit history and external obligations. +1 if credit_history is 'no credits/all paid' or 'all paid' (no track record or just-cleared), +1 if other_payment_plans is 'bank' or 'stores', +1 if existing_credits >= 2, +1 if other_parties == 'co applicant'. Higher = more concerning profile.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines several weak categorical risk signals into a tree-splittable ordinal score.
